scope: Follow-up review of network Worker script semantics, response ownership, certificate generation and proxy cancellation
changes: Both network injection paths share a directive-prologue and hashbang aware inserter; original strict/sloppy mode, ASI and malformed-program rejection remain intact
Recognize standard and legacy JavaScript MIME types; inject successful Worker 2xx bodies, preserve status codes, and abort partial Worker responses
Keep ordinary page scripts out of Chromium Worker rewriting, preserve CSP/CORS and remove the public Blob source hook
Deduplicate paused response events and cancel late fulfillment after target detach, network failure or destruction; abort failed rewrites and close the browser if abort cannot be confirmed
Move production Firefox CA and leaf generation off the main event loop; deduplicate same-host jobs, bound signing concurrency and LRU storage, remove leaf artifacts and cancel work before CA cleanup
Close pending upstream CONNECT on client cancellation; validate actual DNS answers for direct sockets and retain Node's default total upload deadline
Preserve both pinned and system upstream CA bundles when supplied together

finalAdditionalCases.reason: Legacy JavaScript MIME and non-200 successful/partial response cases were added after the full suite; affected paths were then revalidated

certificateProbe.measurementNote: Single local observations of responsiveness, not a statistical throughput benchmark

limits: Native Windows/macOS GPU, font and vendor-kernel behavior remains platform-specific and was not certified on Linux
Network module static dependencies still execute before an entry module body; classic-worker checks do not certify every module graph
Firefox first-instruction limits for blob/data, cached and local-bypass Worker scripts remain documented
Firefox interception still uses Node TLS/HTTP1 rather than native Gecko TLS/HTTP2 fingerprints
Synchronous certificate helpers remain available only for compatibility fixtures; production startup uses the async factory
